evidence: Expected: project/issues/ISSUE-0017.md states that a disabled persistentBrowser control disqualifies a policy, even when another part looks compliant.
Observed: graph.py preserves both enabled=false and mode="never", but _qualifies_for_admin_signin_frequency checks only pb.get("mode") == "never" and ignores pb.get("enabled").
A direct reproduction using a full-admin-role policy with signInFrequency enabled/everyTime and persistentBrowser {isEnabled: false, mode: "never"} produced admin-signin-frequency status "pass".
The existing tests cover absent, empty-mode, and mode=always controls, but not the disabled-with-mode-never representation that exposes this false pass.
findings.remediation: Require the normalized persistentBrowser control to be enabled as well as having mode == "never" (for example, pb.get("enabled") is True and pb.get("mode") == "never"). Add a regression test whose raw control is {"isEnabled": false, "mode": "never"} and assert that the rule fails.
findings.title: Disabled persistent-browser control can satisfy the rule
findings.verification: Run the new disabled-with-never regression test, all admin-signin-frequency cases, the full backend test suite, py_compile, and governance validation against the repaired candidate commit.

limitations: The required full backend suite could not be independently completed because this review sandbox denies loopback socket binding; 129 tests passed and 76 server tests errored during setup.
The exact py_compile check could not be run without writing bytecode. AST parsing all tracked Python sources succeeded but is not equivalent evidence.
Governance validation could not complete because no writable temporary directory was available.
Frontend checks were not run because ISSUE-0017 does not require them and no frontend files changed.
No live Microsoft Graph or tenant validation was performed; the issue explicitly scopes the change to offline normalization and analysis of already-fetched data.
review.summary: The candidate implements the requested normalization fields, coverage union, documentation, fixture, and nine rule scenarios, and the targeted 48 graph/analyzer tests pass. One medium-severity correctness defect blocks acceptance: a persistentBrowser control explicitly marked disabled still qualifies when its stale mode is "never", contrary to the approved issue and causing a false posture pass. Full-suite, exact compile, and governance evidence also remain independently unverifiable in the read-only sandbox.
